Copy or move SharePoint files and folders

Source: R/sp_item_copy.R
sp_item_copy.Rd

These functions copy or move items in a SharePoint document library. Their interface is based on fs::file_copy(), fs::file_move(), and fs::dir_copy():

  • sp_item_copy() copies files. Use sp_dir_copy() to copy folders.

  • sp_item_move() moves (or renames) files or folders.

  • sp_dir_copy() and sp_dir_move() copy or move folders and their contents.

As with {fs}, if new_path is an existing folder, each item is placed inside that folder and keeps its name. Otherwise, new_path is the full path for the new item and its parent folder must already exist. A new_path that ends in "/" must be an existing folder.

new_path can be a path relative to the drive that holds the item, or a SharePoint folder or document library URL. Items can be copied to another drive or site, but they can only be moved within the same drive.

Usage

sp_item_copy(
  path,
  new_path,
  ...,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  wait = TRUE,
  drive_name = NULL,
  drive_id = NULL,
  drive = NULL,
  site_url = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

sp_item_move(
  path,
  new_path,
  ...,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  drive_name = NULL,
  drive_id = NULL,
  drive = NULL,
  site_url = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

sp_dir_copy(
  path,
  new_path,
  ...,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  wait = TRUE,
  drive_name = NULL,
  drive_id = NULL,
  drive = NULL,
  site_url = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

sp_dir_move(
  path,
  new_path,
  ...,
  drive_name = NULL,
  drive_id = NULL,
  drive = NULL,
  site_url = NULL,
  call = caller_env()
)

Arguments

path

A character vector of file or folder paths, or SharePoint file or folder URLs. A relative path must not include the drive name. path can also be a ms_drive_item object or a list of ms_drive_item objects.

new_path

A character vector of new paths, or SharePoint folder or document library URLs. new_path must be length 1 or the same length as path. A relative new_path is in the same drive as the item it is paired with.

...

Arguments passed on to get_sp_drive

drive_url

A SharePoint Drive URL to parse for a Drive name and other information. If drive_name is a URL, it is used as drive_url.

default_drive_name

Drive name string used only if input is a document URL and drive name is not part of the URL. Defaults to getOption("sharepointr.default_drive_name", "Documents")

cache

If TRUE, cache drive to a file using cache_sp_drive().

refresh

If TRUE, get a new drive even if the existing drive is cached as a local option. If FALSE, use the cached ms_drive object if it exists.

cache_file

File name for cached drive or site. Default NULL.

site

A ms_site object. If site is supplied, site_url, site_name, and site_id are ignored.

overwrite

If FALSE (default), an error is returned if an item already exists at the new path. If TRUE, an existing file is replaced. SharePoint can't replace a folder, so sp_dir_copy() works like fs::dir_copy() instead: if new_path is an existing folder and overwrite = TRUE, the contents of path are copied into new_path (replacing any files with the same name). sp_dir_move() has no overwrite argument because a folder can't be moved to an existing folder.

wait

If TRUE (default), wait until each copy is complete. See details.

drive_name, drive_id

SharePoint drive name or ID.

drive

A ms_drive object. If drive is supplied, drive_name, site_url, and any additional parameters passed to ... are ignored.

site_url

A SharePoint site URL in the format "https://[tenant name].sharepoint.com/sites/[site name]". Any SharePoint item or document URL can also be parsed to build a site URL using the tenant and site name included in the URL.

call

The execution environment of a currently running function, e.g. caller_env(). The function will be mentioned in error messages as the source of the error. See the call argument of abort() for more information.

Value

Invisibly returns a character vector with the new path of each item, relative to the drive it was copied or moved to.

Details

Copying is asynchronous

Microsoft Graph copies items in the background. If wait = TRUE (the default), sp_item_copy() and sp_dir_copy() check the status of each copy until it is complete, so they can report an error if a copy fails. Large folders can take a while to copy. If wait = FALSE, the copy may still be running when the function returns, and a failed copy isn't reported.

See also

Microsoft365R::ms_drive_item

Examples

dir_url <- "<link to SharePoint directory>"

if (is_sp_url(dir_url)) {
  drive <- get_sp_drive(drive_name = dir_url)

  # Copy a file into an existing folder
  sp_item_copy("Reports/report.docx", "Archive", drive = drive)

  # Rename a file
  sp_item_move(
    "Reports/report.docx",
    "Reports/report-2026.docx",
    drive = drive
  )

  # Copy a folder to a new folder named "Reports-backup"
  sp_dir_copy("Reports", "Reports-backup", drive = drive)

  # Move a folder into the folder at a SharePoint URL
  sp_dir_move("Reports-backup", dir_url, drive = drive)
}
